subject.title: [Feature/RFC]: Add eval-backed option discovery to avoid premature convergence in route/strategy answers

question: Should OpenClaw adopt option discovery before confident route, strategy, or choice recommendations as a default behavior invariant, and if so what eval boundary should prove it?
rationale: The current code has related search and tool-discipline surfaces, but no existing product contract defines how broad adjacent-option exploration should be or how much extra latency/cost is acceptable.

options.title: Accept eval-first invariant
options.body: Define a narrow generic QA Lab scenario for route/strategy/choice recommendations, then consider the smallest prompt/runtime change that passes it.

options.title: Keep it opt-in
options.body: Treat this as an optional research/best-insight profile or future config surface rather than changing default behavior for all runs.

options.title: Decline core default
options.body: Leave this as model/provider behavior and continue improving search knobs and evidence capture without a new OpenClaw invariant.

recommendation.title: Accept eval-first invariant
recommendation.body: Define a narrow generic QA Lab scenario for route/strategy/choice recommendations, then consider the smallest prompt/runtime change that passes it.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent Codex/web-search maintenance plus release ownership makes this the best available routing candidate for deciding whether the default-behavior bar belongs in core.
